summary: Executed the four requested cases with supporting states allowed. Both require-all cases were proved infeasible at national planning. Both choose-states cases remain inconclusive under their solve limits. No complete plan or realized map was produced.

tests.result: Unavailable: no active project and no activation tool exposed

configuration.conditional_purity: Any pure N, WH or FI contact requires full state coverage in that pure channel; multiple districts within the same pure channel are allowed.

national_stage.note: All three national passes reached their time limits. The following WH pass stopped on an empty plan. Values are rounded as printed in the solver log.

require_all_diagnostic.interpretation: Even the driver's connected-support upper bound for a national district containing Colorado is below the floor under the current distance and state-count limits. Both require-all models were independently reported infeasible by HiGHS.

superseded_attempts.note: These earlier attempts restricted national territory to the original 20 states. Three ended in infeasibility; choose/cap was stopped when the user authorized supporting states. Those results do not describe the final broader scenario.

followups: Improve or warm-start the conditional-purity MILP before another choose-states comparison; the current timeouts do not establish infeasibility.
For the require-all scenario, revisit the Colorado floor or geographic constraints with the user before rerunning. Do not silently remove Colorado or weaken purity.
After a full plan exists, run ZIP realization, refresh the ZIP audit with --audit-only, then evaluate terminal rematching and FEFx. None was reached by these runs.
learned: full_plan's fixed_used bounds fix the first requested slots open but do not close surplus slots. The experiment adapter pairs lower and upper slot bounds to implement exact counts.
Conditional state-channel purity can be enforced with the existing contact variables while permitting same-channel district splits.
The assignment exporter uses the literal district label other for residual opportunity; it is not an empty string.
Each run records its commands, input hash and implementation hashes. The implementation included the pre-existing uncommitted worktree changes, which were preserved.
